MARKET.head: Bordeaux holds 41% of weekly fine wine trade value; Burgundy gains
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux claimed 35.7% of traded value. Burgundy and Champagne followed closely behind
takeaways: Bordeaux claimed 41% of the week's traded value on the Liv-ex fine wine market, extending its lead.
Burgundy's share rose from 15.7% to 20.8%, with Domaine de la Romanee-Conti and Domaine Leflaive top-traded by value.
Champagne's share fell from 13.0% to 8.5%, while Tuscany claimed 11.6% led by Soldera and Sassicaia.

MARKET.head: Top Burgundy wines grow scarce in China as producers tighten allocations
MARKET.summ: Some of Burgundy’s most sought-after wines are becoming harder to source in China, importers told Vino Joy News, as smaller harvests and tighter allocations constrain supply
takeaways: Importers in China report tighter supplies of DRC, Leroy, Leflaive and Domaine Gros Frère et Sœur since July, per Merveille Business CEO Li Yajun.
Fine West CEO Wu Xianghua says Leflaive cut 2024-2025 output and reduced China allocations, so fewer bottles reach the market.
Shanghai Boyun's Lin Jianbing says leading Burgundy prices have fallen considerably over two years, contradicting claims of demand outstripping supply.

MARKET.head: English sparkling wine grows fast but faces oversupply and falling grape prices
MARKET.summ: After a decade of rapid growth and rising international recognition, English sparkling wine faces the challenge of turning enthusiasm into sustained sales
takeaways: Wines of Great Britain reports English vineyard plantings rose 510 percent between 2005 and 2024, reaching 4,841 hectares.
Global English wine exports rose 35 percent from 2023 to 2024, with the US counted as a leading market for some producers.
Overproduction has pushed grape prices down, with Dermot Sugrue saying they dropped to historic lows by the end of 2025.

MARKET.head: Monichino Wines to close after 64 years as Victorian cellar door sales fall
MARKET.summ: According to reporting by The Weekly Times, Monichino Wines at Katunga in the Goulburn Valley will close its doors after 64 years in business. “It’s all become too hard , the costs have blown out, with the red tape and taxes and everything else,” Cellar door manager Anna Sergi told The Weekly Times. The newspaper explained that...
takeaways: Monichino Wines at Katunga in the Goulburn Valley will close after 64 years in business, selling its property and vines.
Owner Anna Sergi cited blowout costs, red tape and taxes; the winery had survived a tornado and pandemic restaurant closures.
Bigibila Winery in Moonambel reports cellar door trade down 40 per cent in six months, owners Peter Bicknell and Jillian Henderson say.

MARKET.head: Sustainability information lifts willingness to pay for fungus-resistant PIWI wine
MARKET.summ: This study investigates how providing consumers with information about sustainability impacts their preferences and willingness to pay for wine made from fungus-resistant (PIWI) grapes. Main headlines Methods Results Conclusion To help sustainable fungus-resistant (PIWI) wines grow beyond a small niche market, wineries and...
takeaways: A study tested whether telling consumers about sustainability impacts changes their preferences for fungus-resistant (PIWI) grape wine.
Its finding: sustainability information is enough to drive consumer interest and boost the value of PIWI wines.
The authors advise wineries to use clear, straightforward sustainability messaging to move PIWI wines beyond a niche market.

MARKET.head: Guangdong lychee ice wine sells out online after APEC dinner menu circulates
MARKET.summ: A Guangdong lychee wine became an unexpected online hit after it was served alongside two Changyu wines at the APEC welcome dinner in Shenzhen, with its producer reporting a more than 93,000% jump in revenue at one online store
takeaways: Yueli Lychee Ice Wine, from Guangzhou ShunChangYuan in Conghua, was served at the APEC welcome dinner in Shenzhen.
After the November 18 menu circulated online, one Tmall flagship store reported roughly 5,000 orders within two hours.
The producer says one online store's revenue rose 93,393.10%, though the comparison period was not specified.

MARKET.head: Weekly drinks roundup covers Jim Beam pause, record-low wine output, and product launches
MARKET.summ: This is VinePair’s Booze News Weekly Roundup, where we gather the hottest headlines and product releases every Friday for a snapshot of what’s happening in the beverage alcohol industry. This week, we have updates on the continued production pause at Jim Beam’s main facility, dismal estimates for the 2026 global wine...
takeaways: VinePair's Booze News Weekly Roundup gathers the week's beverage alcohol headlines and product releases every Friday.
Coverage includes an ongoing production pause at Jim Beam's main facility and dismal estimates for 2026 global wine production.
Other items cover Stoli's return to the U.S. and Modelo's deal with the NCAA.

MARKET.head: DBR Lafite merges China winery and sales under Leo Wang
MARKET.summ: Former Pernod Ricard executive Leo Wang will oversee Domaine de Long Dai and the group’s China sales team as longtime winery chief Charles Treutenaere prepares to leave
takeaways: Domaines Barons de Rothschild Lafite appointed ex-Pernod Ricard executive Leo Wang to run its Chinese winery and national sales as one unit.
Wang becomes managing director of Domaine de Long Dai in Shandong, the group's first single leader for both China operations.
Long Dai general manager Charles Treutenaere, nine years at the estate, leaves at year end and will assist the handover.

MARKET.head: WineGB to exhibit English and Welsh wines at Amsterdam trade fair in January 2027
MARKET.summ: English and Welsh wine has moved from a niche market to one of the most dynamic cool climate categories in Europe. Producers are gaining international attention for sparkling wines, as
takeaways: WineGB, the national association for English and Welsh wine, will exhibit at Wine Professional in Amsterdam in January 2027, with the UK government's GREAT programme.
The association aims to introduce Dutch buyers, importers, sommeliers and distributors to UK producers and their sparkling, still white, rosé and red wines.

MARKET.head: California Table Grape Commission hires new marketing director for North America
MARKET.summ: The California Table Grape Commission has added Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie as its Global Marketing Director for Canada, Mexico, and Central America
takeaways: The California Table Grape Commission has hired Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie as Global Marketing Director for Canada, Mexico and Central America.
She was previously CEO of the Center for Produce Safety and international marketing director for American Pistachio Growers.
She will work with importers and retailers to expand promotion and demand for fresh California table grapes.

MARKET.head: Wine Australia opens funding call for grape and wine innovation projects
MARKET.summ: Wine Australia is today launching a competitive call for innovative eligible projects to secure funding from the Research & Innovation Fund (RIF) which is part of the Australian Wine Future Fund (AWFF). The organisation said innovative and groundbreaking projects tackling the wine industry’s most critical challenges will be...
takeaways: Wine Australia launched an expression of interest for its Research & Innovation Fund, part of the Australian Wine Future Fund.
The fund targets $35 million over five years via grants and partner co-investment for vineyard, product and efficiency projects.
The current round closes 23 December 2026, with assessments in early 2027 and quarterly rounds after that.

MARKET.head: ProWine Mumbai to showcase India's wine and spirits market to global producers
MARKET.summ: India’s growing appeal to international wine and spirits producers will take center stage at ProWine Mumbai this month, as rising disposable incomes, demand for premium drinks and new trade agreements open opportunities in the market
takeaways: ProWine Mumbai runs November 18-19 at Jio World Convention Centre, expecting 200+ exhibitors and 6,000 trade visitors.
Twelve national pavilions and over 1,000 wine and drinks brands will be showcased, with spirits, beer and no-alcohol drinks included.
Tariffs on some imported wines and spirits are set to fall as free trade agreements with Australia, UK, NZ and the EU take effect.

CULTURE.head: Schloss Johannisberg tops World's Best Vineyards 2026 ranking, up from second
CULTURE.summ: Germany’s Schloss Johannisberg has been named the world’s best vineyard for 2026, rising from second place last year. Only one Chinese winery made it onto the extended top 100 list
takeaways: Germany's Schloss Johannisberg in the Rheingau was named World's Best Vineyard for 2026, rising from second place last year.
The ranking, run by William Reed and announced November 18 in Chile, weighs history, architecture, hospitality and visitor experience alongside wine.
Bodegas Ysios in Spain's Rioja ranked second and Chile's Montes third, with Silver Heights from China the only Chinese winery listed.

CULTURE.head: Wine Australia launches educator network with 10 specialists across eight Asian markets
CULTURE.summ: Wine Australia has launched the ‘Australian Wine Specialist Educator Program’, a new initiative set to bring trusted professional wine educators together across Asia to deliver “engaging, locally relevant Australian wine education”. It explained that at the heart of the program is the Australian Wine Specialist Educator Network...
takeaways: Wine Australia launched the Australian Wine Specialist Educator Program to bring local wine educators across Asia together.
The inaugural network includes 10 educators across eight key Asian markets, building on existing relationships in China.
Educators will teach Australian wine using Wine Australia's Australian Wine Discovered platform, with Australia visits planned for 2026 and 2027.

CULTURE.head: Newbridge Wines' Bendigo Fiano wins People's Choice award again
CULTURE.summ: A Fiano by Newbridge Wines in Bendigo has taken out the trophy for Best Aromatic White Wine for the second year in a row at The People’s Choice Wine Awards. Organisers explained the show is judged by wine enthusiasts rather than by qualified winemakers or wine industry professionals. “When we planted ten years ago almost nobody...
takeaways: The People's Choice Wine Awards, judged by wine enthusiasts rather than industry professionals, named Newbridge Wines' 2026 Fiano Best Aromatic White for a second straight year.
Heathcote's Peregrine Ridge Winery won Best Shiraz for a second year running, with its 2014 Shiraz taking the trophy.
Condie's 2021 The Max Shiraz took the Public's Choice Red, ahead of a three-way tie for runner-up.

CULTURE.head: ProWine Shanghai shows China's wine buyers seeking distinctive, regional, casual-occasion wines
CULTURE.summ: China’s wine market is becoming more selective, more diverse and less dependent on formal drinking occasions, according to exhibitors at this year’s ProWine Shanghai
takeaways: Exhibitors at ProWine Shanghai say Chinese buyers are becoming more selective, looking beyond quality and price for distinctive wines.
The three-day exhibition drew over 620 exhibitors from 34 countries and regions and 21,800 trade visitors.
Wine consumption in China is widening beyond business banquets and gifting to casual restaurants, wine bars and drinking at home.

CULTURE.head: ASVO ratifies four regional directors, including two new appointments, for 2026/27
CULTURE.summ: The Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology (ASVO) has announced that the appointment of two new directors at its annual general meeting last week “strengthens the board's national presence and builds its depth of skill as the association moves into 2026/27”. “The new board comprises an excellent diversity of experience...
takeaways: Mark O'Callaghan, a Victorian winemaker and consultant, and Lane Williams, head viticulturist at Leeuwin Estate, were appointed as new ASVO regional directors.
The Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology ratified four regional directors at its AGM, each for a three-year term.
Chrissie Smith and Alana Seabrook continue as regional directors for NSW/ACT and SA respectively, with Sam Scarratt serving as ASVO president.

CULTURE.head: Melbourne Polytechnic opens lower-cost wine degree places from 2027
CULTURE.summ: Melbourne Polytechnic is expanding access to tertiary viticulture and winemaking education through Commonwealth Supported Places in its Bachelor of Agriculture and Technology (Viticulture and Winemaking) from 2027. As Victoria's only provider of undergraduate degrees in viticulture and winemaking, Melbourne Polytechnic “plays a...
takeaways: Melbourne Polytechnic will offer Commonwealth Supported Places in its viticulture and winemaking bachelor degree from 2027.
It is Victoria's only provider of undergraduate viticulture and winemaking degrees.
Eligible domestic students' annual contribution falls from $23,160 to $4,908 for the major.

CULTURE.head: Wine's cultural status slipping as sales fall and mocktails rise
CULTURE.summ: I was re-reading an article titled “Is Free Trade Passé?” that the economist Paul Krugman wrote back in 1987 and it got me thinking about what’s happening in the world today. Here is my report. >>><<< Is Free Trade Passé?
takeaways: The writer argues wine is losing its status as the default social beverage, as sales of wine and alcohol have fallen sharply.
He observes fewer bottles on restaurant tables and some venues offering longer mocktail lists than wine lists.
He compares wine to coffee, which has shifted from a default choice to one option among many.

CULTURE.head: VinePair's Keith Beavers reflects on American wine in 2026 and ways to celebrate it
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks. Tucked between the Vosges Mountains and the Rhine River in northeastern France, Alsace is one of the most distinctive wine regions on earth, and is home to centuries of family winemaking, some of France’s most certifiably organic vineyards, and a...
takeaways: Keith Beavers, host of VinePair's podcast Wine 101, reflects on American wine in 2026 in this episode.
The episode is sponsored by Wines of Alsace, promoting the French region's Riesling, Pinot Gris and Crémant d'Alsace.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Highlights: The Weyborne Estate Oriana Brut 2022 England
NEWSLETTERS.summ: We had a sneak preview of this wine last year, when Weyborne released ‘The Golden Spur’, which is
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Weyborne Estate's Oriana Brut 2022 from England is a blend of 46% Chardonnay, 53% Pinot Noir and 1% Pinot Meunier.
The wine was previously previewed last year as 'The Golden Spur', an earlier-disgorged version of the same wine.
Wineanorak scores the Oriana Brut 2022 94/100, priced at £48 direct from Weyborne, at 12% alcohol.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Vinography Unboxed: Week of 11/16/26
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly dig through the pile of wine samples that show up on my doorstep, asking
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: Beaujolais Anew
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The 2026 release of that wine we love to hate and hate to love, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Beaujolais Nouveau was pushed onto the world stage by Beaujolais vignerons, with Georges Duboeuf marketing it beyond France by the 1970s.
Beaujolais Nouveau is released worldwide on the third Thursday of November, with Gamay grapes and carbonic maceration yielding low-tannin, fruity wines.
Lapierre in Morgon labels its wine a Vin de France, nicknamed "Raisins Gaulois," because French law bars cru wines from the Beaujolais Nouveau label.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Cabernet Franc in the Press: November 2026
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Livermore wins Region of the Year, Wine Spectator profiles Loire Cabernet Franc, Decanter takes a cross-border look at Ontario and New York, and much more
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Wine Enthusiast named California's Livermore Valley its 2026 American Wine Region of the Year in its annual Wine Star Awards.
Livermore Valley is known for Sauvignon Blanc and Cabernet Franc, which its regional association named its signature white and red varieties in February 2025.
A Cabernet Franc claimed top honours at Maryland's Governor's Cup.

NEWSLETTERS.head: More Than Skin Deep: A Grape with a Colourful Past
NEWSLETTERS.summ: A colourful tale of the grape that was born to dye and the father-son team behind it
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Blanc de Noirs Champagnes are white wines made from black grapes, Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier, because their juice is colourless and skin contact is minimal.
Garnacha Tintorera, also called Alicante Bouschet, is a red-fleshed grape bred by Louis and Henri Bouschet in 19th-century France to add colour to wines.
The featured Pago Casa Gran 'Reposo' 2024 from Valencia, Spain, is a blend of 60% Garnacha Tintorera, 20% Syrah and 20% Monastrell.

NEWSLETTERS.head: What the Hell Do They Mean?
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Let’s play wine tasting note bingo, here’s TMC’s handy guide
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: The author says "funky" is a positive term for natural wine fans but a red flag for mainstream drinkers, and Berlin and New York reportedly banned it.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Burgundy Region Quietly Absorbing This Year’s Rising Prices
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Discover how the Burgundy wine market quietly absorbs rising prices in 2026, revealing new trends and steady demand for fine wine collectors
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Comité des Vins de Bourgogne figures show Burgundy white wine sales rose 0.4 per cent in the year to July 2026, while red fell 4.9 per cent.
Mâconnais bulk prices fell: Mâcon-Villages Blanc down 9 per cent and Bourgogne Blanc down 13 per cent, per regional agriculture office figures.
Pouilly-Fuissé gained 22 Premier Cru climats from the 2020 vintage, the first in the Mâconnais, with more from 2025.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Many Sins Of Wine Critics
NEWSLETTERS.summ: In the exciting (other adjectives are available) times we’re living in, we’re often told that writing is passé, people just don’t bother reading words anymore. A few journalistic outlets, especially in the financial press, seem to have finally come clean about the seriousness of their reporting, by auto-summarising their pieces...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues that wine critics should be only slightly more knowledgeable than their target audience, not far beyond it.
Atkin says undisclosed conflicts of interest matter beyond payments, including dining, friendships and shared politics.
Atkin criticises wine reviewers spending about 30 seconds per wine, comparing it to judging a movie by its trailer.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Find Rare Shizz With Orpheus Alerts!
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Some (more!) exciting news, folks: As many of you already know, sometimes wines get featured on here that are pretty rare. I’m talking about the kind of stuff that either doesn’t make it to the big platforms, or, if it does, is either priced astronomically or is gone in milliseconds. Understandably, that can be somewhat […]...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude is partnering with Orpheus Alerts, part of Orpheus Intelligence Labs Inc., to help buyers find rare wines.
Orpheus monitors sources like local-language catalogues, merchant pages, consignment notices, restaurant sales and estate inventories.
Users create alerts using natural-language descriptions or uploaded images, and Orpheus notifies them when a matching wine is found and connects them to the seller.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: Spain ranked fifth by volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy but only a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
For value, Spain dropped to sixth in China, below New Zealand, with per-liter value above only Chile among the top eight sources.
The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing, with Guangzhou next on November 6, showcasing value-priced Spanish wines like DCOOP's Airén and Tempranillo.
